RC7 fixes two interruptions in automatic prompt context: local preparation consuming JEV's
selection time, and an explicit task switch leaving the current turn attached to an older packet.

- Context operations now have a 10-second cooperative allowance. JEV selection gets up to
  3.5 seconds after preparation, within the remaining allowance. Individual provider deadlines
  remain bounded by the project profile. The managed prompt hook allows 15 seconds for fallback
  delivery and reader cleanup. Receipts separate preparation, index, selection, current provider
  call time and total time; replayed calls do not count as new provider latency.
- Creating, resuming, forking or revising a task records when context needs refreshing. The normal
  `context-route --task <current request>` command refreshes for that task without a failed first
  attempt. It reuses the repository index and retains the same turn's call/byte allowance and
  expansion ceiling. Original packets and receipts remain intact. A task change during selection
  refuses stale delivery; ambiguous native turn usage remains unallocated across tasks.
- The managed launcher now admits the documented `context-index` and top-level help commands.

Adoption remains deliberate. Update the pin and reconcile the local runtime at a safe seam. The
managed prompt handler changes from 10 to 15 seconds. Reconciliation and host approval of that
exact definition are required for RC7 prompt qualification; retaining the old 10-second handler
is unsupported and can cut off fallback delivery. Existing JEV disclosure and model settings remain project-owned; no credentials or
new hosted permissions come with this release.
An expired or exhausted turn stays local-only until a new prompt is observed. If the host skips
the hook, reconcile that observation gap; refreshing context does not silently renew spending.

This release is qualified locally at the operator's request, with source tests, typechecks,
legacy wheel checks, installed archive proof and bounded synthetic live JEV evidence. GitHub
Actions is skipped for this publication; it remains enabled for future work. Local qualification
does not establish Linux-host behavior, physical-device outcomes or token/time savings in ordinary
development.
